utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case IT-08-91-T, the Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Good afternoon to everyone. I, first of all, note for the record that in the absence of Judge Delvoie, we're sitting today under Rule 15 bis. May we have the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Joanna Korner and Crispian Smith for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. On behalf of defence of Mr. Stanisic, Slobodan Cvijetic and Deirdre Montgomery.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. For Zupljanin Defence this afternoon appearing, Igor Pantelic, Dragan Krgovic, and Miroslav Cuskic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday it was brought to my attention that we had forgotten not to move out of private session, and I'm wondering whether the -- what way you are now headed, Mr. Krgovic. We -- we -- we need to revert to private session or whether we remain in open session. Could you -- could you assist me in that regard?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I propose that we stay in open session for a time. I will try to avoid mentioning the position, the name, or any tasks performed (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: before it goes out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And I'm also advised that yesterday afternoon, as if by magic, yesterday evening just after the adjournment the translation of -- of the document in question appeared. So we are now ready to -- to continue. I take it, Ms. Korner, that you have seen it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, we have. Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. (redacted) before I invite Mr. Krgovic to continue -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Witness, before I invite Mr. Krgovic to resume his cross-examination, I remind that you're still on your oath. Yes, Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To avoid any mention, I will address you as Witness. I'm not going to use any determinant. I'm trying to formulate my questions so that you can answer with a yes or no, and if there are questions where you have to explain what you did, then we will go into private session. And please signal whenever you feel that you may divulge your identity by an answer, and I will seek to go into private session. Is that clear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-213 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday I showed you this document. It's still before you. Have you had a chance to look at that it? First of all, I showed you the first and last page. Now, go to page 2 of the document, please. Does this document, in principle, contain everything that a document of such nature should contain?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-213 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Does this seem as an authentic document, dating from that period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-213 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if there's no objection, I would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm not at all sure that the witness can testify as to its authenticity or not, but have I no objection to it going in, because the signature and stamp have been identified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D52, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please take a look at page 12 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That would be page 11 in the English version. I don't know how it is in e-court. Could be the next page. That would be page 12 in the English version. I think ... I apologise, just a second, please. Well, since, in e-court, pages are not the same as the document pages, that would be the next page in e-court, please. In English. The B/C/S version is okay. So I apologise. The versions are different. In English, the exhibit number is 2D02-1191.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 12 in the English version, I think. It is page 11 in English, after all. That would be the right page. Yes, thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 2, that would be the last sentence, there is a piece of information concerning the number of received and sent dispatches, and it says that in the first nine months, in 1991, covered by this report, 180, 160.168 dispatches and 335.858 have been received. In other words, 188.168 were received and, 39.858 were sent. Do you agree? Do you agree that this is stated in the document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-213 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it. It is stated so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You have no reason to believe that this is incorrect?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-213 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not have any information that this would be incorrect.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't want to object. But I don't think the witness is being asked whether this document is one that the witness has ever seen before. Because, as you notice, I didn't deal with the content except when I was dealing with it. And if the witness has not seen it before, then this just really a method of just reading out what's in the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I may respond. My examination is linking up with Madam Korner's examination. She broached the subject of the number of dispatches that went through the witness's hands in a certain period of time, and it is my intention to clarify this matter, to see the period that we are dealing with, to compare 1991 to 1992. And on the basis of that, to ask the witness to confirm certain facts. This is the gist of my using this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, again, I mean, I don't want to delay matters. I think that it was put to the witness yesterday that dispatches were matters that were done by telecommunication and were sent by Mr. Rakovic. And that's a slightly -- there was a clear distinction drawn between detaches and correspondence that came for the chief. I don't know that the witness gave any evidence which suggested that the witness had any knowledge of the numbers. But as I say, I mean, rather than delay matters, I'm just putting that down for the record, that how helpful the witness can be over this is something that's completely different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I think I see where you are going Mr. Krgovic. But, of course, as Ms. Korner says, the content to separate - how should I describe it? - the system from the contents. There's no point by way of -- in the course of asking questions, in essence reading out the contents of this document which the witness had no hand in making. But -- so if you -- if you would bear that in mind, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will bear that in mind, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you have any knowledge that, for instance, in 1991, there was a large number of dispatches which reached you, which went through the place where you worked at? By meaning -- by meaning -- by saying "the place," I mean the institution that you worked at.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-213 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned that in -- during that year, there was a large number of dispatches. I cannot say it was 180; it could have been 150 or 120. It was a large number. And I cannot tell you whether 31 or 41.000 were sent. I'm not certain about the exact figure, but there was a large number of dispatches.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: When I mentioned these figures, I mean roughly. But this would be a large number which corresponds to the figure mentioned in the report. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-213 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's take a look at, please, P595. Can we see it on e-court, please. Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to give you a hard copy for convenience. Please take a look at page 1 of this document. This is a report on the work of the centre from the 1st of January until the 30th of June, 1992. And then take a look at the last page of this document, please. Is this Mr. Zupljanin's signature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-213 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And the stamp of your centre; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-213 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Please go to page 17 in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That would be page 12 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And at the bottom of the page, you will hear [as interpreted] that there were 9.956 dispatches received and 9.686 sent. 728 coded dispatches, and 898 coded dispatches were sent out, and 2.297 dispatches were in transit. Can you agree that this statement is here stated in the first six months of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-213 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this report covers the first six months. The previous report covered nine months. I did not do anything with respect to this document, but I know that there was a large number of such dispatches.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Now, please take a look at another document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P621.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I will give you a hard copy for your convenience. Please take a look at the first page. That would be a report on the work of the centre from -- for the period from 1st of July to 30th of September, 1992. And then take a look at the last page, please. Is there a signature? Is this Mr. Zupljanin's signature?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, the penultimate page. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Although it is not typed, I recognise Chief Stojan's signature. Let me take a look at the stamp. And the stamp is authentic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at page 14.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In English, that would be page 31. In the Serbian version, that would be ERN 0074-9631.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So we are dealing with another three months. The previous document dealt with 1991, nine months, then I showed you a report covering the first six months of 1992, and then another, which covers three months of 1992. It states here that 1996 uncoded dispatches were received and 162 coded were received. 1.396 were received, and 43 were sent. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-213 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It states so here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: If we compare 1991 and 1992, the same periods, in 1991, we will see in the first nine months in peacetime there were 228.026 dispatches received. And in the first nine months in 1992, 27.151, which would be 10 per cent of the number from 1991. So this number is much smaller than the figure from peacetime.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-213 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, on the basis of the information that communications service prepared, this would be so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And when you voiced your estimates on the number of dispatches that went through your hands, that figure would be how far you could understand or recall. You gave us an average number of dispatches that went through your hands, not the exact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-213 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The individuals who took care of communications were definitely better placed to give estimations and figures involved?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-213 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only estimations, they had specific figures that they kept records of.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Precisely. That's what I meant. They had the exact numbers and accurate records; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-213 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor showed you a document yesterday, which is P569, that I will show you now. This is a fax message, is it not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-213 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not a fax message. It's a dispatch.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: But it was sent through a fax machine.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-213 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't want to go into the work that -- done by the encryption people, but a fax would have a -- or, rather, there should be a DD reference at the top there. It should state "communications centre." I don't think that it went through a fax.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Can you direct your attention to the middle part of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And can this number in the middle be enlarged, please. Above where it states "page 2."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Can you see it now? 13th June 1992, 2943 [as interpreted] and this number, 39155. Are you familiar with this number?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-213 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not. And I don't know what sort of procedure was used in the communications centre once they received a dispatch. But the number, 078, is the Banja Luka prefix. But I didn't work in the communications centre in order for me to be able to know what means they used.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: That's clear.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we call up 65 ter document 230.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: This is a report from 1992. Can you help us here? This reference 11-1/02, that's the general crime department reference, is it not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-213 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: This is a report on the arrest and arraignment of certain individuals of Serb ethnicity who had committed crimes against the Muslim population. And you see it is stated at the bottom: "Chief of centre, Stojan Zupljanin." But the signature is not his, is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-213 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it isn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: As discussed yesterday, the separate services which sent their documents out, when doing so, they would have the chief sign it, and then they would be sent out independently of you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-213 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Independently of me, but the deputy chief was able to sign such correspondence, and not the individual services.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps I should have said a high-ranking official who had a certain position and certain powers within the centre.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-213 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The number, 3400/92 in the upper right-hand corner, that's the number of the crime registry where the criminal report was basically filed. So it was the 3400th criminal report filed that year. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-213 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the number, and that's the crime register, right, KU.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The date is the 28th of August, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-213 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And the stamp is that of the centre, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-213 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I wish to tender this document into evidence, unless there are any objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D53, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: In answer to the Prosecutor's questions, you spoke of certain references or designations placed on documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us look at P123, MFI.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I have the usher's assistance in handing you this set of documents. These are photo copies that will facilitate the examination. It is much easier to have documents in front of you. I'm interested in the document marked with number 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at page 1 of the document, and I'm interested in the top part of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And can we have the same portion enlarged on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: This is a document from the Security Services Centre, public security centre of -- station of Sanski Most, which was sent to the chief. It's not a dispatch. In fact, you called it differently. What was the term that you used?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-213 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A strictly confidential document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: There's a handwritten note here. It seems to me that these are Mr. Zupljanin's initials, are they not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-213 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There where 02 is written, it is his initials, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: It says here the corps HQ and the MUP are to be notified. And below that, we have Stojan Zupljanin's initials. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-213 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: We have 02 reference at the top again standing for the general crime department.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-213 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Crime department is 02. In other words, who is to be charged with the task.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: It follows from here that when Stojan Zupljanin received the dispatch, he immediately forwarded it to the corps HQ and the head office of MUP; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-213 [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the reference, he tasked the sector 02 with this, told them what to do, and placed his initials next to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry. Could the witness just read out the whole thing so we get an accurate translation of what is on the letter? I simply -- I think that Mr. Krgovic's was a slight summary. So if the witness just reads it out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Sorry, you're talking about the manuscript note in the top right corner?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You heard Ms. Korner. Could you read out the entire handwritten part.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-213 [Resumed]
utterances.text: "02," underlined, "notify the corps headquarters, or command, and MUP."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And below that is Mr. Zupljanin's signature, is it not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-213 [Resumed]
utterances.text: His initials.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: What else is written there to the left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-213 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says: "Djukic." And the rest, I can't make out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know of a Djukic who worked for the general crime department at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-213 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I believe that there was a Dusko Djukic, an inspector in the crime service.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: What we have there is a different handwriting on the same letter, slightly to the left, and in somewhat darker ink.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-213 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter notes we didn't hear Mr. Krgovic's last parts of the question because the microphone was switched off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, could you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I asked the witness if he could read the part of the text, and (redacted) answered no.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Both sexes, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to shorten the procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Witness. When I was drawing your attention to the handwriting part in darker ink, I asked you if you could read what was written there, and the interpreters didn't hear this part of my question. So could you please repeat your answer, since I've repeated it myself. But can you make out what is written there in the darker ink?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-213 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I cannot.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Can you assist us with the following.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, if Mr. Krgovic is moving to another document, in the light of the witness's answers, can I move now that that document be fully exhibited, as opposed to being MFI'd?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P123, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're interested in 2D38, MFI. It's under 2 in the set of documents you have. Look at page 2 of the document. There's a handwritten note which says on the 27th of August, 1991 ... there is something handwritten there. Can you make out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-213 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Next to number 11, 230. That's an entry I made, in my own hand.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please turn to page 2 of the document. We have the stamp there of the centre, and the signature of the chief, Zupljanin; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-213 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And it does seem to be an authentic document from the period.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-213 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to have this document fully exhibited now, the one that has been MFI'd, if there are no objections.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No objection at all, Your Honour. I'm just trying to, however, find the part by number 11 in which the witness said it was the witness's writing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's in the original in a handwritten number 11, 11-230.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. No objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have 2D40, MFI.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: That's behind tab 4 for your benefit. This is a 5th of December, 1991 report. And can you please look at the last page of document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Before you go on, I don't think that the last item was formally entered. So it's admitted and marked as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D38, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Look at the last page of the document, please. We have the seal, or the stamp of the centre, and Stojan Zupljanin's signature. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-213 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And next to SSUP under "copies delivered to," we have someone's handwriting. Do you know who it belongs to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-213 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: By its format and by the signature it bears, does it tally with the documents you had occasion to see through your work at the institution?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-213 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. By the format and by the look of it, I should say it does, but I have never seen this document before.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next, 2D2026 -- 1264. Can we please have it on e-court. 2D02-1264.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Please take look at the document on your screen. It will appear any moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 2D02-1264.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: This is a dispatch. I would like -- what I'm interested in is this designation 11-1/04-76. 11 was the designation of the communications centre. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-213 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: This went from this organ under the name of Stojan Zupljanin; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-213 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Which doesn't mean that Stojan Zupljanin signed this document personally. Most probably, communications centre chief signed him, since it comes from this organ. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-213 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know who signed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: One general question: Once a document is brought to the communications centre and handed over to the person working there, that person cannot -- when typing the message, the dispatch, they cannot type the signature; they cannot transfer the image of the document from the original. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-213 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Communications centre cannot receive a dispatch to be sent if it's not signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: But when they do transfer it, they cannot transfer the original signature. It just inserts a signature block. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-213 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, just the signature block.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Although somebody else, pursuant to their authorisation, signed the dispatch, the recipient cannot see at the place of destination what the signature is. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-213 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's -- that is something I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Just another question: You discussed the circumstances during war while you worked, and you mentioned the period where there were power cuts. What I'm interested in: Do you recall that, in 1992, when the corridor between Krajina and the rest of Bosnia-Herzegovina was cut off, there were longer power cuts and people would throw out the food from their refrigerators and their freezers because there was no electricity. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-213 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Was that in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-213 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. This is -- this is all -- well, I apologise. Just a second. Thank you, I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Krgovic. Mr. Cvijetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no questions for this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I have only one matter to deal with in re-examination. Before that, however, I'm just wondering whether I can return to the slightly vexed subject of whether Mr. Krgovic would like to suggest to the witness, if that's the case, that the identification of Mr. Zupljanin's voice is right or wrong. It's returning to the old question that I raised some weeks ago, but I do think, in the light of this witness, whether, if there is -- it is disputed, that ought to be made clear now. I don't -- I don't think we're likely to have a better witness on that subject.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, has this witness been confronted with the intercepts?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, you will recall that in the evidence in chief and in the proofing note, the witness listened to - and I gave the numbers - and positively identified -- identified is the wrong word - I keep saying that - it's recognised the voice of Mr. Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: On how many tapes? Forgive me for --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I said it fairly quickly, so Your Honours can be forgiven for forgetting it. It's a total of - one, two, three, four - five.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So you are now asking Mr. Krgovic to indicate whether he will accept the witness's testimony that (redacted) did recognise Stojan Zupljanin's voice on these five tapes?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Exactly. And I think it is appropriate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in the light of your decisions date 16th of December and yesterday's decision concerning the intercepts, I believe that we -- I have no need to stipulate in respect of this witness. I believe that this matter has been resolved in your previous decisions, and we have the same situation that we used to have before.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can I just say it's not quite the same, Your Honours. Your Honours have admitted the intercepts; they are part of the evidence. That, in itself, doesn't specifically deal with the accuracy or otherwise of who is speaking. And, in any event, it is -- this evidence, if nothing else, is solid, corroborative evidence of the evidence given by those who dealt with the intercepts. And when Your Honours come to consider, at the end of the day, the weight that you attach to that evidence, this is, we submit, something that's quite important. I -- I'm not -- I don't want to re-argue all the matters I argued last time. I am merely raising it at this stage, because I think it is appropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, the -- as we recall the ruling that we gave, and Mr. Krgovic's understanding of that ruling is consistent with what we thought we had said, the -- if the Defence, for whatever reason, chooses not to challenge or test this bit of evidence, the -- we would have thought that the evidence stands and certain consequences would follow. I shouldn't say would. Certain circumstances are likely to follow. And I would have thought that experienced Defence counsel would be acutely aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, well -- I'm not going to labour the point. I just thought this was an appropriate time mention it again.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Witness, I just want, for a moment, to go back to the document that you were asked about, which is P595, I think. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And we'll need page 11 in the English, and page 17 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And it's paragraph 5.1 that I want you to look at when it comes up on the screen. I'm afraid it's a very bad copy, so if we can try -- it's talking about -- and this is the 19 -- the six months of 1992, to June, the functioning of the communications system and the cryptographic protection. Now, I just want to, first of all, before we look at this, to see whether we've all understood correctly. The communications that you have been calling dispatches were dealt with by the communications department, is that right, under Mr. Rakovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-213 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But documents which were couriered --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry, could we go into private session for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Witness, this report refers to the reduced number of professionals working in the CSB. Is that something that you know about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-213 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not concerned with personnel policy, and I didn't know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I know you weren't concerned with personnel policy, but did you yourself notice that people leaving --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, no, we're not in America, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you yourself notice that people were leaving?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-213 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally would, on occasions, know of somebody leaving; but that they were leaving en masse, no, I didn't know that. Because work did not suffer. It was done by the people who were doing the job.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So you don't understand, then, the reference in this report to the reduced number of professionals, which, apparently, was also a problem?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-213 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. I won't pursue that further. Then it talks about repairs and establishments of links where there had not been any before in Donji Vakuf, Krupa, and Kupres SJBs and then due to war operations, there were constant interruptions in telephone and telegraph links with some SJBs; Kupres, Donji Vakuf, Krupa, Glamoc, Bihac, Teslic, Grahovo, Drvar, Sipovo, Mrkonjic Grad. From your --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry. I think back into private session, please, for the next question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Witness, we thank you for your appearance before the Tribunal and the assistance that you have afforded. And we wish that you have a safe journey back to your home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I take it that there are no matters that need engage us further afternoon, in which case the witness need not be escorted out of the court before the Court rises. And we would take the adjournment to ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I think it's Courtroom II on Monday morning at 9.00. And I trust that everyone has a safe weekend. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 8th day of March, 2010, at 9.00 a.m. 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 3.27 p.m.,
